causes.what: A rolling rollout of app version 412 to 413 is producing database errors on each app host as it lands; the database itself is healthy.
dns-01 CPU jumped from about 22% to about 94% at 10:20:45 and DNS query time went from about 24 ms to about 1,800 ms, a separate fault that may add to the slow responses.

ruled_out: db-01 and db-02 (CPU ~23%, I/O wait 8% and 3%, replication lag 2.6 s and 1 s, connections flat at 52-68) are healthy
cache-01 is healthy (hit rate 93.7%, 2.5 ms response)
network or switch fault is unlikely because every host still answers ping with 0% loss on the hosts checked
the 5xx and slow-response alerts on web-01 to web-04 and lb-01 are symptoms of the app errors, not independent faults

evidence.claim: db-01 looks normal: CPU 23%, I/O wait 7.9%, replication lag 2.6 s, ping OK
db-02 looks normal: CPU 23.8%, I/O wait 3.5%, replication lag 1.0 s
app-01 db error rate went from 0 to 8.93 at 10:19:42
The onset is staggered by host over about 5 minutes while db-01 connection count stayed flat at 52-68
app-01 version moved 412 to 413 between its 10:16:57 and 10:21:57 samples (sampled every 5 min)
app-02 version moved to 413 between 10:17:52 and 10:22:52
app-04 version moved to 413 at 10:25:51, after its 10:20:51 sample of 412
app-03 still read 412 at 10:21:58 although its errors started at 10:22:02; the next version sample was not yet available, so the version link for app-03 is unconfirmed
dns-01 query time about 24 ms at 10:19:05, then 1766 ms at 10:20:05, still about 1700 ms

next_step: Check the deployment log for the 413 release: confirm the rollout order and times and roll back, or pause, the release on the remaining hosts. Also look at what is using dns-01's CPU (for example a query flood), as a separate task.
